whatWorks: The moss / bone / warm-grey family over a near-black ground is genuinely quiet and organic. Across all twelve seeds nothing goes garish, the ground never lightens, and the three hues sit in one key rather than reading as three unrelated colourways.

Token identity survives the state rows. 5003 and 5396 are recognisably the same object in neutral, stress and recovery: the vertical axis, the member family and the palette rotation all persist, so a state change reads as the same relic under different conditions rather than as a reroll.

Every token is held on one vertical axis near the canvas centre, and the mid-extent seeds (5134 neutral, 5920) already deliver exactly the compact figure with a clear quiet margin that the composition direction asks for.

At 120px the marks are individually legible rather than mush: no seed collapses into grey noise, edges stay crisp and the silhouette survives the downscale. That legibility floor is what any move toward finer linework has to hold onto.
5134 neutral has a real stem descending below the mass, the one place in the set where the growth has an origin and a direction rather than being an unanchored star.

findings.whatFails: Nothing in the set divides. The set splits into two layouts and neither is a frond: 5003, 5658, 6444 and 5396 are full-length straight bars crossing at a common point, all the same length and weight from end to end; 5527, 5789, 5920, 6051, 6182 and 6313 are chevrons stacked in parallel horizontal bands of equal size. There is no parent member, no shorter child hung off it, and no angular turn between generations anywhere in the twelve.
findings.why: The brief's subject is the logic of growth -- a stem that divides, and divides again, each division smaller and turned slightly from the last -- and the direction asks for growth expressed as branching interval. Uninterrupted bars through a centre are an asterisk, and equal chevrons on parallel rows are a woven band; both are single-generation layouts that state repetition instead of division, so the frond reading never starts.
findings.specificChange: Replace the flat member list with an explicit recursive generator of 3 to 5 generations: each child's length is 0.55-0.70x its parent's, each child is rotated a fixed 15-30 degrees from its parent's heading, and each child is anchored to a point along its PARENT's span -- never to the canvas centre. Remove the parallel-band layout entirely so a member's position is always inherited rather than gridded.
findings.keep: Keep the strict centring and the single dominant vertical axis, keep the descending stem that 5134 neutral already has and extend it to every seed as the recursion's root, and keep the current overall footprint of the mid-extent seeds so the figure still reads as one growth.

findings.whatFails: The strokes are heavy enough that overlap fills. 6182 is a solid green rectangle of stacked zigzags with almost no ground showing through, 5527 and 6051 read as opaque carved plaques, and the 5003 and 5658 bars are wide struts rather than lines. In the 512 single the members have merged into one continuous silhouette with no internal linework left at all.
findings.why: The brief says fine linework throughout, delicate rather than heavy, with the drawing carried in line rather than in mass, and the density direction says no filled mass anywhere. Heavy strokes plus mirrored overlap manufacture exactly the filled mass that was ruled out, and the result reads as a mask or a totem plaque rather than as thread.
findings.specificChange: Decrease stroke width to roughly one third of current -- target 1.0-1.5px at 256px for generation 1 -- and taper it per generation so each successive division is about 0.75x the width of its parent, generation 4 landing near hairline. Increase member count by 2-3x to hold the figure's presence, and cap total ink coverage so no seed exceeds about 20% of its bounding box filled.
findings.keep: Keep the 120px legibility that the heavy strokes currently buy: after thinning, the outermost generations may fade but the primary armature must still resolve as a distinct shape at 120px, and no seed may degrade into an undifferentiated grey haze.

findings.whatFails: In all four state columns, stress is the largest, densest and brightest of the three rows, while recovery is nearly a duplicate of neutral. 5003 stress adds rays and reaches the tile edge; 5396 stress adds a whole diagonal layer over the neutral verticals; 5265 stress is visibly bigger and brighter green than neutral; and 5003 recovery versus 5003 neutral is close to indistinguishable at browse size.
findings.why: The brief states the opposite: recovery extends the branching outward and multiplies its divisions, while stress retracts the form back toward a bare central armature. As rendered, distress makes the plant bloom and repair does nothing, so the one narrative the market transformation carries is being told backwards -- and two of the three states collapsing into each other means the token effectively has two states, not three.
findings.specificChange: Invert the drive: increase generation count and maximum reach as recovery rises, and decrease both as stress rises, removing the outer one to two generations under stress so only the root stem and its first division survive. Separate neutral from recovery by at least one additional generation and a 15-20% increase in outer reach, so the three rows are three distinguishable silhouettes at 120px.
findings.keep: Keep the token identity that already holds across the rows -- the axis, the seed's characteristic turn angle and its palette rotation must stay fixed under every state -- and keep neutral's current footprint as the middle of the range so the three states bracket it rather than all growing from it.

findings.whatFails: At 120px the twelve seeds resolve into two templates plus a palette rotation. 5789, 5920, 6051 and 5527 are the same stacked chevron block at different brightnesses; 5003, 5658 and 6444 are the same crossed-stick star; 6182 is the chevron block in green; 5265 and 6313 are the same shapes shrunk. Cover the seed labels and most of these are not tellable apart at browse size.
findings.why: The variation strategy asks tokens to differ first in how far the branching has extended, then in density of members, then in palette rotation -- three ordered axes. What is actually varying is scale and colour, so the primary axis is doing almost no work, and the identity anchors are additionally broken because the stacked-band family is not a centred radiating figure at all.
findings.specificChange: Spread the seed-driven parameters across genuinely visible ranges: branching turn angle across 12-40 degrees, generation count across 2-5, and members per division across 2-5, and make turn angle the primary per-seed axis so silhouette outline changes before brightness does. Add a per-seed root count of 1-3 stems. Require any two seeds' 120px silhouettes to differ in outline, not only in fill.
findings.keep: Keep the shared family signature -- dark ground, centred vertical figure, moss-and-bone pairing -- so the twelve still read as one collection, and keep the existing extent variation as the secondary axis rather than deleting it.

findings.whatFails: Occupancy swings wildly and clips at the top end. 5396's horizontal bars run out of the tile and are cut flat by the left and right edges, and 5003's near-vertical rays are cut by the top edge; 5789's thin lines also exit the frame. At the other extreme, 5265 and 6313 occupy under a third of their tile, and the 512 single sits as a small dark form in a very large empty field.
findings.why: The composition direction asks for a compact radiating figure held near the centre WITH clear space at the frame edge, and the negative-space direction wants that emptiness to read as where growth has not yet reached. A member sliced by the viewBox reads as a rendering fault rather than as a choice, and a form at a third of frame reads as an undersized crop rather than as generous emptiness.
findings.specificChange: Pin the rendered figure's bounding box to a fixed band of 60-78% of the shorter frame dimension for every seed and every state, scaling the whole composition to fit rather than clipping, and inset by at least 8% of frame on all four sides so no member ever touches or crosses the viewBox. Narrow the seed-to-seed occupancy spread to that band instead of letting extent drive raw size.
findings.keep: Keep the quiet open margin around the mid-extent seeds and keep the centre-anchored placement; the fix is to normalise scale, not to enlarge every token until the margin closes up.

findings.whatFails: The palette rotation has an unbounded luminance spread against the ground. 5265 is dark olive on near-black and nearly disappears at 120px, and the 512 single has so little separation from the ground that its outline has to be hunted for. At the other end 5003, 5658 and 6444 are near-white bone at close to full contrast, so the same collection contains tokens that shout and tokens that vanish.
findings.why: The palette intent is low contrast so the linework reads as thread rather than as structure, but low contrast is a relationship, not a licence for the darkest rotation to fall below visibility. In a browse grid an invisible token is not quiet, it is a hole -- and the thumbnail intent requires a radiating star of fine lines to survive as silhouette at 120px in every rotation.
findings.specificChange: Declare a minimum luminance separation between the primary generation-1 members and the ground -- at least 22-25 L* -- and darken or lift each palette rotation to sit inside a bounded window rather than free-ranging; simultaneously cap the brightest rotation so bone members stay below about 82 L*, narrowing the collection's total luminance spread. Let only generations 3 and beyond fall toward the low-contrast floor.
findings.keep: Keep the near-black ground exactly as it is and keep the moss-and-bone pairing with its low-contrast character; this is a floor and a ceiling on the members, not a call to raise overall contrast or brighten the field.

overall: The palette, the centring and the state-to-state identity are sound, and the marks hold up at 120px -- but what is on screen is not a frond. Both layouts present are single-generation: full-length bars crossing at a point, or chevrons stacked on parallel rows, with no parent-to-child division, no shrinking reach and no angular turn anywhere in the twelve seeds, so the one idea the brief is built on has not been implemented. That absence is compounded by weight: the strokes are heavy enough that mirrored overlap fills into opaque plaques (6182, 5527, the 512 single), which is the filled mass the density direction explicitly rules out, and it pushes the reading toward mask and totem rather than thread and growth. The market rows are running backwards -- stress is the fullest, brightest, most extended state in all four columns while recovery is a near-duplicate of neutral -- so the collection currently narrates distress as flourishing. Underneath that, the seed axis is doing almost no work: at 120px the twelve fall into two templates separated mainly by brightness and scale, while framing swings from members sliced off by the viewBox (5396, 5003) to forms occupying under a third of the tile (5265, the 512 single), and the darkest palette rotation drops below the point where the silhouette can be seen at all. The order of repair is recursion first, then stroke weight, then the state direction; the things to protect while doing it are the ground, the hue family, the centred axis and the 120px legibility the current heavy strokes are buying.
